name: Windtrail Park (Windtrail Park Apartments)
headline: CARE Communities is renovating Windtrail Park, its 50 ground-floor two- and three-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 60% AMI (10 for seniors 55+) at 2120 Bridgefield Lane and 945 Rolland Moore Drive in Fort Collins, by selling it to a new tax credit partnership. It won a 2025 federal 4% award from CHFA backed by Housing Catalyst bonds.
why_it_matters: A local nonprofit is recapitalizing its own 2001 tax credit property with a $4.45M seller loan, city CDBG and capital-tax money and a state grant, adding air conditioning and in-unit laundry and resetting affordability for 60 years; it shows how tariffs and Buy America rules widened a small preservation deal's gap by about $2M.

status.label: Ownership moved to the new partnership (assessor record); rehab start not confirmed
status.detail: Larimer County parcel records (run 2026-10-08) list Windtrail Park LLLP, registered 2025-09-10, as owner of both parcels, which indicates the acquisition closed (inferred; the deed date and price were not found). CARE targeted a late-February 2026 closing and a 2026-03-02 construction start; no permit, groundbreaking or completion record was found.

next_step: Watch for City of Fort Collins building permits and a completion or lease-up notice from CARE Communities.

key_numbers.meaning: 5 at 30%, 25 at 40%, 16 at 50% and 4 at 60% AMI; 44 two- and 6 three-bedroom units; 10 reserved for seniors 55+.
About $8.4M over 10 years; no state credit. CARE budgets $6,983,894 of tax credit equity.
Issued from Fort Collins' 2025 private activity bond cap of $11,184,752, which the city assigned to Housing Catalyst.
$371,475 per unit, including $5,153,825 of acquisition cost and $8,542,446 of construction; CARE carries back a $4,450,000 seller loan.

facts.value: 2120 Bridgefield Ln, Fort Collins 80526 (CHFA). CARE says 40 units are at 2120 Bridgefield Lane and 10 across the street at 945 Rolland Moore Drive; parcels 9723371001 and 9723371002, Lots 1 and 2 of CARE Housing at Windtrail Park PUD; census tract 001111
Family, acquisition/rehabilitation; in a QCT; not in a DDA or SADDA; Section 8 column marked No

Built in 2001 with low-income housing tax credits and federal HOME funds (from DOLA, the City's CDBG program and the state), 13 residential buildings, a clubhouse and a community garden; all units are ground-floor homes; not renovated since construction

New heat pumps that add air conditioning for the first time, washers and dryers in every unit, interior and exterior paint, new flooring, cabinets and windows, ENERGY STAR fixtures and appliances including tankless water heaters and LED lighting, more accessible units and paths, bike storage, community Wi-Fi and a clubhouse expansion; built to Enterprise Green Communities 2020 criteria
A two-bedroom, one-bath unit rented for $565 to $1,254 depending on income, against a 2024 Q3 Fort Collins average of $1,643, per CARE's application
Windtrail Park LLLP (registered 2025-09-10); CARE Windtrail Park LLC registered the same day at CARE's address (inferred general partner)

background.text: CARE built Windtrail in 2001 as a tax credit property; the city backed the original development with a $901,000 award in 1999.

Deal structure: CARE sells the property to a new partnership it controls, carries back a $4,450,000 seller loan, and says the proceeds and earned developer fee will be reinvested in its five-year pipeline. The sale price is not public; the budget's acquisition cost rose from $4,551,250 to $5,153,825 mainly because the appraised value went up.
The rehab resets the 2001 affordability restrictions for at least another 60 years.
CARE first sought bonds in March 2024 for a combined Greenbriar and Windtrail rehab under one partnership ($16M of bonds, $10,812,010 from the city); in 2025 it filed Windtrail alone.

Fort Collins received two 2025 bond cap requests; its committee and the Affordable Housing Board (May 2025) backed Windtrail as the complete, on-time, in-city request and recommended assigning the cap to Housing Catalyst.

Costs rose from $16,575,311 (February 2025) to $18,573,766 (December 2025) because of tariffs, Build America Buy America rules tied to the federal CDBG money, interest rates and higher appraised value; a hoped-for $500,000 from a Larimer County preservation fund never materialized. CARE cut landscaping, asphalt, garden and clubhouse scope.

CARE budgets $300,000 for temporary resident relocation and compares the job to its 2022 occupied rehab of the 84-unit Swallow Road Apartments, where residents moved temporarily while units were renovated; an occupied rehab at Windtrail is inferred, not stated.
